description: Data layer: create the dance_orgs Supabase migration (19_dance_orgs.sql) with the required schema, public-SELECT RLS and service-role-only writes, indexes; the DanceOrg TypeScript type; and the server-side getDanceOrgs() data-access function. Foundation for FEAT-002 (carousel reads orgs) and FEAT-003 (sync writes orgs). No dependencies.
steps: Create supabase/migrations/19_dance_orgs.sql. Columns (exact): id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), name TEXT NOT NULL, slug TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, website_url TEXT NOT NULL, logo_url TEXT, logo_source_url TEXT, logo_verified BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false, sort_order INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(), updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(). Use CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS. Follow the DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_policies WHERE tablename='dance_orgs' AND policyname='Public read dance_orgs') THEN CREATE POLICY 'Public read dance_orgs' ON dance_orgs FOR SELECT USING (true); END IF; END $$; pattern from supabase/migrations/17_dance_crews.sql. Precede it with ALTER TABLE dance_orgs ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;. Do NOT add INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies (service role bypasses RLS — add a SQL comment stating writes are service_role only). Add CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS dance_orgs_slug_idx ON dance_orgs (slug); and CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS dance_orgs_sort_order_idx ON dance_orgs (sort_order);.

Create lib/dance/types.ts (new file). Do NOT edit lib/dance/constants.ts (it is import-free by design per its header comment). Export interface DanceOrg { id: string; name: string; slug: string; website_url: string; logo_url: string | null; logo_source_url: string | null; logo_verified: boolean; sort_order: number; created_at: string; updated_at: string; }

Create features/dance/services/danceOrgsService.ts. No 'use client' directive (server module). Import { createClient } from '@/lib/supabase/server' and type { DanceOrg } from '@/lib/dance/types'. Export async function getDanceOrgs(): Promise<DanceOrg[]> that does: const supabase = await createClient(); const { data, error } = await supabase.from('dance_orgs').select('*').order('sort_order', { ascending: true }); if (error) { console.error('[getDanceOrgs]', error.message); return []; } return (data as DanceOrg[]) ?? [];

Run `npm run typecheck` from c:\website\GrooveSystem and confirm zero errors. The migration SQL is not applied by the build — confirm it is syntactically balanced (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, the DO $$ … END $$ block, both indexes).
acceptance_criteria: supabase/migrations/19_dance_orgs.sql exists with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dance_orgs, all 10 required columns, RLS enabled, a 'Public read dance_orgs' SELECT policy in a DO $$ IF NOT EXISTS guard, no write policies, and both indexes.
lib/dance/types.ts exports DanceOrg matching the columns exactly.
features/dance/services/danceOrgsService.ts exports async getDanceOrgs(): Promise<DanceOrg[]> using createClient() from @/lib/supabase/server, ordered by sort_order ASC, returning [] on error.
`npm run typecheck` passes with zero errors.
verification: cd c:\website\GrooveSystem && npm run typecheck  # zero TS errors

Confirm 19_dance_orgs.sql has CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, ALTER TABLE dance_orgs ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, the DO $$ IF NOT EXISTS SELECT policy guard, and both CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS statements.
findings: FEAT-001 (data layer) complete. `npm run typecheck` = zero errors. Deliverables: (1) supabase/migrations/19_dance_orgs.sql — CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dance_orgs with all 10 columns (id UUID PK DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), name TEXT NOT NULL, slug TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, website_url TEXT NOT NULL, logo_url TEXT, logo_source_url TEXT, logo_verified BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false, sort_order INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(), updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()); ALTER TABLE dance_orgs ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; DO $$ IF NOT EXISTS guard creating policy "Public read dance_orgs" FOR SELECT USING (true); NO write policies (SQL comment states writes are service_role only, since the service role bypasses RLS); indexes dance_orgs_slug_idx and dance_orgs_sort_order_idx. SQL verified syntactically balanced: 2 dollar-quote markers (even), 11 open / 11 close parens. (2) lib/dance/types.ts exports `interface DanceOrg { id: string; name: string; slug: string; website_url: string; logo_url: string | null; logo_source_url: string | null; logo_verified: boolean; sort_order: number; created_at: string; updated_at: string; }` — import it via `import type { DanceOrg } from '@/lib/dance/types'`. logo_url and logo_source_url are nullable (string | null). (3) features/dance/services/danceOrgsService.ts exports `async function getDanceOrgs(): Promise<DanceOrg[]>` — server-only (NO 'use client'), imports `{ createClient } from '@/lib/supabase/server'` (anon key, RLS applies, public SELECT works), awaits createClient(), selects '*' ordered by sort_order ASC, returns [] on error. FOR FEAT-002 (carousel): import via `import { getDanceOrgs } from '@/features/dance/services/danceOrgsService'` and call it inside the Server Component (the dance page), then pass the plain DanceOrg[] as props to the 'use client' carousel component — do NOT import this server fetch inside a client component. A logo_url of null (or an empty/missing row) means render the text-pill fallback using the org's `name`. FOR FEAT-003 (sync): writes MUST use the service-role key (createAdminClient from @/lib/supabase/server, or a direct @supabase/supabase-js client built with SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY) — the anon client cannot write because no write policies exist. NOTE on policy quoting: the spec's inline pseudo-SQL wrote `CREATE POLICY 'Public read dance_orgs'` with single quotes, which is invalid Postgres (a policy name is an identifier, not a string literal). I followed the 17_dance_crews.sql pattern the spec explicitly pointed to, using a double-quoted identifier `"Public read dance_orgs"` in CREATE POLICY and a single-quoted string literal in the pg_policies WHERE check. This is the only deviation and it produces valid, syntactically balanced SQL.
